newsitem.title: USA: Interstate Bakeries Q4 met/exceeded plan.
newsitem.headline: Interstate Bakeries Q4 met/exceeded plan.

text.p: Interstate Bakeries Corp said Thursday its results for the fiscal fourth quarter ended May 31 met or exceeded its expectations.
Earlier, it reported earnings of $0.77 a share, up from $0.23 a year ago after a $0.15 charge.

"The fourth quarter results met, and in some instances exceeded, our expectations," Charles Sullivan, chairman, said in a statement. "This is further proof that our growth strategies are on track and moving forward."
Sullivan added that, as a percentage of net sales, Interstate Bakeries' operating income margin grew to 7.3 percent in the fourth quarter from 4.5 percent a year ago.
He added bread and cake sales grew modestly.

"While still not where we want to be in unit sales volume, our net dollar sales results continued to improve in the fourth quarter as they have throughout the year," Sullivan said. "Our strongest segment continues to be branded white bread with the Wonder white brand leading the way."
In snack cakes, Sullivan said there was still room for improvement, but added the company was seeing "some positive movement," particularly in its Hostess brand.
Looking ahead, Sullivan said Interstate Bakeries expected to continue its solid growth, especially through brand building and the addition of San Francisco French Bread Co.

"We know we must build sales volume in our branded bread and cake, as well as improve our operating margins through further cost containment and operating efficiencies," Sullivan said. "While much work remains for us, this past year stands as an example of what we can accomplish and we believe we are well positioned for many challenges that await us."
